_realFields: Document number, type, supplier, material, plant, quantity, unit, rate, value and delivery date all exist in the sandbox: API_PURCHASEORDER_PROCESS_SRV (A_PurchaseOrder, A_PurchaseOrderItem) and API_PURCHASEREQ_PROCESS_SRV (A_PurchaseRequisitionHeader).
_simulatedFields: heldWith, step, rule, reason and hoursWaiting are SIMULATED. They describe the approval workflow (SAP release strategy and the work item sitting in someone's inbox). The sandbox exposes no workflow work items, no approver assignment and no reason an approval is stuck, so these are invented here.
_note: value is always quantity x rate, so the numbers on screen add up. hoursWaiting is a fixed number rather than a live clock, so the demo reads the same every time it is opened. In a real system it would be now() minus the work item creation time.

documents.rule: Orders above 1 crore need two approvals
documents.reason: The second approval was triggered by the order value. The approver has not opened it yet.

documents.rule: Orders above 25 lakh need two approvals
documents.reason: The approver has been away since 2 September and no stand-in was named, so nobody can act on it.

documents.rule: Requests above 10 lakh need purchasing approval
documents.reason: Waiting for the cost centre owner to confirm the budget before purchasing can approve.

documents.rule: Service orders above 10 lakh need one approval
documents.reason: Sitting in the queue behind eleven other items.

documents.rule: Orders above 5 lakh need one approval
documents.reason: Normal queue, nothing is blocking it.
